paper_title: DIY-MKG An LLM-Based Polyglot Language Learning System
caption: DIY-MKG reliably expands the vocabulary with low sensitivity to the language and the starting word. For each language, 10 opaque curves represent vocabulary sizes obtained from 10 different starting words, and one solid curve represents the average of the 10 curves. The standard deviations across languages and starting words are small, indicating fairness for all language learners. The diagonal gray line represents the upper-bound of vocabulary size, assuming all words in each iteration have not yet appeared in the vocabulary. While the real expansion rate is lower, the vocabulary does not saturate after 500 iterations. Therefore, DIY-MKG can reliably help the language learner to expand their vocabulary by consistently introducing new words.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of iterations and vocabulary size for three languages: Spanish, Korean, and Japanese. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Iterations," has a linear scale with a range of 0 to 500, units of iterations, and tick labels at regular intervals of 100. The y-axis, labeled "Vocabulary Size," has a linear scale with a range of 0 to 5000, units not specified, and tick labels at intervals of 1000. The plot displays four lines: a gray diagonal line representing the upper-bound of vocabulary size, and three colored lines for each language - Spanish (blue), Korean (orange), and Japanese (green) - each consisting of a solid line representing the average vocabulary size and 10 opaque curves representing individual vocabulary sizes obtained from different starting words. The blue line starts near (0,0) and ends near (500, 3000), steadily increasing with a consistent slope. The orange line starts near (0,0) and ends near (500, 2900), also steadily increasing with a consistent slope. The green line starts near (0,0) and ends near (500, 2900), similarly increasing steadily with a consistent slope.
